clue.text: The first person to cycle on Bournemouth's front using both feet

indicators.note: in an across clue the following pieces are placed on, i.e. after, the B
the front of the word Bournemouth's is its opening letter

parts.note: the first person singular pronoun is I
to cycle is to pedal a bike

explanation.surface: A cyclist pedals along Bournemouth's seafront with both feet on the pedals.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-footed creatures are described as walking upright on two legs, the literal sense of the Latin-derived adjective.

clue.text: Flower without carbon would be flatter

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the word for flatter goes around carbon

parts.note: to flatter someone is to butter them up
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A flower without carbon would be flatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means minus, but here it is the old sense of outside, so 'flatter' wraps round the carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow meadow bloom of the ranunculus family is a common wild plant.

clue.text: Remedy provided by a general practitioner?

definitions.text: Remedy provided by a general practitioner?

parts.words: Remedy provided by a general practitioner?
parts.note: a GP is a family doctor, but read as a practitioner of everything in general, the cure offered would be a universal one

explanation.surface: A family doctor prescribes a treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all is a single treatment for every ill, a universal remedy.

clue.text: Broadcast ordering support for divisional leader in heroic action

indicators.note: the leader of divisional is its first letter
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An order broadcast to support a divisional commander in a brave operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' scatters ORDERING plus D (the leader of 'divisional'); 'support for' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless bravery or daring deeds are heroic action, an old phrase now used humorously.

clue.text: Timer failing to open security device

indicators.note: failing to open means the word for timer loses its opening letter

parts.note: a clock is a timer

explanation.surface: A timer that won't open a safe's security mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastening worked by a key protects doors, a basic security fitting.

clue.text: Walked when demon shaver showed the way

parts.note: Sweeney Todd is the Demon Barber of Fleet Street, a shaver of throats
showed the way means led

explanation.surface: Someone walks off while a fearsome barber leads the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the fictional 'demon barber' of Fleet Street in London, hence 'demon shaver'.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk with short unsteady steps, like a small child.

clue.text: No primary' colour employed by rising animal painter

indicators.note: primary means first, so the colour is placed first in the build

parts.note: a tint is a colour
O is nought, i.e. no or nothing

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the animal is written upwards

parts.note: an otter is an animal

explanation.surface: An artist known for animal paintings who never uses a primary colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns OTTER to RETTO; 'primary' sets TINT ahead of O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian Renaissance artist Jacopo Robusti is known by his nickname, a famous Old Master.

clue.text: Urge to plunge into river? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: into first suggests the plunge goes into the river
quite the reverse swaps the roles, so the river goes inside the plunge

parts.note: to plunge is to dive
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An urge to plunge into a river, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' plus 'Quite the reverse' puts R inside DIVE, not DIVE inside R.
explanation.definitionFit: To press or push someone forward is to urge them on.

clue.text: Rest of story somewhat blue

parts.note: a story is a fib or lie
feeling somewhat blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: The rest of a story is rather sad.
explanation.definitionFit: A short nap or recline on a bed is a period of rest.

clue.text: Old-fashioned Cockney disliked supporting daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the daughter
a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: disliked means hated

explanation.surface: A Cockney father disliked his daughter's old-fashioned ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop H, so HATED becomes 'ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of date belongs to a past era, no longer in vogue.

clue.text: Clear return offered by gold, import

indicators.note: return asks for the word for clear to be taken back to front

parts.note: to clear a sum after deductions is to net it
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A financial return is offered by gold and imported goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads 'Clear' backwards. 'import' is the noun meaning drift or purport, not goods brought in from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of a speech is its general meaning or drift, which is what its import is.

clue.text: Elected to serve, in substance in Europe perhaps

indicators.note: in here asks for the first piece to sit inside the word for substance

parts.note: the substance of a book is its content
a party elected to serve is in, i.e. in office

explanation.surface: Someone elected to serve in Europe, in substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is one of the great landmasses of the world, an example of the category.

clue.text: Prompt retirement by top mathematician

indicators.note: retirement suggests going backwards, so the word for prompt is read in reverse

parts.note: an actor's prompt is a cue
a lid is a top on a jar

explanation.surface: A top mathematician is prompted to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' is the reversal signal: a retiring actor withdraws backwards off the stage, so the prompt is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek geometer of Alexandria, author of the Elements, is the classic example of a mathematician.

clue.text: Course warning notified as anticipated

parts.note: on a golf course the warning shout is fore
notified means told

explanation.surface: A warning on a course was given just as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: On a golf course, players shout 'fore' to warn people a ball is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell is to predict, so something predicted was anticipated in advance.

clue.text: Suffer appalling danger in scene of tumult

parts.note: to suffer something is to bear it

indicators.note: appalling signals the letters of danger are put in a dreadful new order

explanation.surface: Someone suffers terrible danger amid a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where bears were baited became bywords for rowdy chaos and uproar.

clue.text: Striking result from the Belfry?

parts.note: the Belfry is a famous golf course, but read literally a belfry houses bells, and a struck bell gives a loud ringing sound

explanation.surface: A remarkable result at a golf tournament at the Belfry course.
explanation.walkthrough: The Belfry is an English golf course that has hosted the Ryder Cup, which tempts a sporting reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud metallic ringing noise is what a struck bell makes.

clue.text: Constituent of potato starter a surprise

parts.note: an eye is a bud on a potato's skin
a starter or opener is the first item

explanation.surface: A potato dish served as a starter turns out to be a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revealing that shocks you into new awareness is a revelation or surprise.

clue.text: Beater's assistant in the forefront

parts.note: the beater is the heart, which a device helps keep time; the runner who sets the speed leads in the forefront

explanation.surface: A grouse beater's helper walks at the front of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a heart-regulating device and a runner who sets the speed are leaders of rhythm.

clue.text: Revived when given a drink

definitions.meaning: being served another round of drinks

explanation.definitionFit: Being restored in vigour and having one's glass topped up both use the same word.

clue.text: Place arranged at court for a wealthy sort

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of at court are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A place is arranged at court for a rich person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose power derives from riches is a rich ruler or wealthy type.

clue.text: Get a kick from riding gelding in safe harness

parts.note: a jockey riding a horse is said to be up

indicators.note: harness means the word for safe holds the letter for gelding

parts.note: safe means sure
g is the racing abbreviation for gelding

explanation.surface: A rider gets a thrill from a gelding in a secure harness.
explanation.walkthrough: In racecards, a jockey 'up' is riding, and g marks a gelding, a castrated horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rise or burst of increase is a kick upwards.

clue.text: Head cook out of one ingredient

indicators.note: an ingredient goes into a dish, so one letter goes inside the cook

parts.note: a cook is a chef
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A head cook makes a dish from a single ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader or boss of a group is its principal person.

clue.text: Game confined in it extremely lively, but put down in a clumsy way

indicators.note: in a down clue, put down means the last piece is placed below
confined in means the game goes inside the word it

parts.note: nap is a card game

indicators.note: extremely means the first and last letters of lively

explanation.surface: A lively game is confined, then put down awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap (napoleon) is an old card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unsuitably or awkwardly is acting clumsily.

clue.text: Trim sail, mistakenly through faulty hearing

indicators.note: mistakenly signals the letters of trim sail are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A sailor trims the sail wrongly because he misheard an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' reorders TRIMSAIL. 'hearing' is a legal hearing, not the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial voided because of an error is a legal hearing that went wrong.

clue.text: Cleans up round quarter and sulks

indicators.note: round means the word for cleans up surrounds the quarter

parts.note: cleans up a floor means mops
E for east is one of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: Someone mops up a quarter and sulks.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood gloomily is to sulk.

clue.text: Send away for instructions

definitions.meaning: to dispatch money or a case to another body
terms of reference given to a committee

explanation.definitionFit: Dispatching payment and the brief given to a body share one word.

clue.text: Run through barrier on motorway when reversing

indicators.note: on in an across clue sets the barrier after the motorway piece
reversing applies to the motorway, whose name is read backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written M and I
a pale is a fence or barrier

explanation.surface: A driver crashes through a barrier while reversing on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway north from London; 'when reversing' turns it round, and 'on' puts the fence after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something with a spike or sword is to run it through.

clue.text: Booked performances

definitions.meaning: being a book, namely the book of the New Testament after the Gospels

explanation.definitionFit: A book of the Bible and turns on a stage share the same name.

clue.text: Parking regulation almost broken by Eugene, the doctor's assistant

indicators.note: broken by means the other pieces are split open with a name inserted

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: almost means the word for regulation loses its last letter

parts.note: an edict is a decree or regulation
Eugene Aram was an 18th-century murderer made famous by a Bulwer-Lytton novel

explanation.surface: A parking rule was flouted by someone called Eugene, who assists a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene Aram was a real 18th-century schoolmaster-murderer. 'almost' trims the last letter from the regulation; 'broken by' splits P and that trimmed word apart for the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained medical worker who gives emergency care helps out alongside physicians.

clue.text: Execute preliminary drawing for vessel

indicators.note: to execute is to behead, so the word for a preliminary drawing loses its head

parts.note: a sketch is a rough preliminary drawing

explanation.surface: An artist makes a preliminary drawing of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execute' means behead here: take the first letter off SKETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing boat is a type of ship or vessel.

clue.text: … all the perfumes of Arabia will not ______ this little hand" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: … all the perfumes of Arabia will not ______ this little hand" (Macbeth)

parts.words: … all the perfumes of Arabia will not ______ this little hand" (Macbeth)
parts.note: Lady Macbeth's line from the sleepwalking scene; the missing word means make fragrant or pleasant

explanation.surface: A quotation from Lady Macbeth trying to clean her bloodstained hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To make the hand smell pleasant again is to render it fragrant and agreeable.

clue.text: Arrested and run in, having offended

indicators.note: in means the letter for run goes inside the word for arrested

parts.note: arrested in the sense of halted means stayed
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A culprit was arrested and run in by police after offending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrested' means checked or halted, not seized by police.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander from the right path is to sin or go wrong morally.
